intro: A TV cooking contest: who takes part, what the rounds are, and how to tell it with the passive voice.

palabras.consejo: The j sounds like h: «hu-RA-do». It is a group, but it takes the singular: «el jurado decide».
The feminine is «presentadora». They present the show and talk to the guests.
It works for men and women: «el finalista», «la finalista». It is who reaches the last round.
Feminine: «la favorita». It is also an adjective: «mi plato favorito» is the one I like best.
Feminine: «aficionada». It comes from «afición». It is the opposite of «profesional».
It also means «proof»: «no hay pruebas». It comes from «probar».
The first r is strong: «RRE-to». You say «aceptar un reto» or «superar un reto».
You say «hacer un ensayo» and «ensayar». It is also a short opinion text.
It has «semi-» (half): «semifinal», «semicírculo». After the semifinal comes the final.
It ends in «-ción», like «puntuación». It comes from «clasificar»: to sort into groups.
It is also the object you serve food on. «Un plato típico» is a traditional dish.
It is masculine: «el postre». You say «de postre tomo fruta».
It is regular. In the passive: «fue eliminado». You can also eliminate a stain or a mistake.
You say «premiar con un viaje». The stressed syllable is the last one: «pre-MYAR».
Future of «elegir», third person: the «á» marks the future.
Plural of «finalista», someone who reaches the last round.
Past tense of «ensayar» for «yo»: the accent on the «é» marks it.
Third person plural of «eliminar», to remove or knock out.
Future of «volver» for «yo»: the «é» marks the future.
The infinitive «intentar» with «lo» attached; the stress stays on «tar».
The «x» sounds like «ks» here: PROK-si-mo.
Future of «publicar», third person: the «á» marks the future.
Masculine form of «ganadora».
Past participle of «premiar», to give a prize.
Past participle of «elegir»; the «g» sounds like «h».
Past participle of «anunciar» in the plural; it agrees with the nouns.
Future of «anunciar», third person: the «á» marks the future.
Months are written in lowercase in Spanish.
A «foco» is a lamp that lights a stage or a studio.
«Estudio» can mean study or studio; here it is the recording room.
Imperfect of «calentar» for «ellos»: the action went on in the past.
A strong light that dazzles, from «resplandecer».
Plural of «encimera», the flat surface in a kitchen where you cook.
Plural of «cuchillo»; the «ch» sounds like «ch» in «church».
Imperfect of «remover»; the «í» breaks the diphthong: re-mo-BI-a.
«Salsa» is a sauce; it can also be the music and dance.
Imperfect of «respirar»: an action that went on in the past.
A «gota» is a drop of liquid, like a drop of rain.
Caramel is sugar cooked until golden.
The «í» breaks the diphthong: ka-I-a, in two syllables.
Imperfect of «sonreír»; the «í» means two syllables.
Plural of «miembro», a person who belongs to a group.
Third person plural of «cortar» in the past.
The «ll» in Spain sounds like «y»: cu-CHI-yo.
Third person of «hundir» in the past: it went down.
«Decepción» comes from «decepcionar», to let someone down.
«Extremo» is the far end or edge of something.
Feminine of «presentador», the person who hosts a show.
Feminine plural of «levantado», agreeing with «manos».
Infinitive of «repetir», to do or say again.
Past participle of «fallar», to fail or break down.
«Intento» comes from «intentar», to try.

piezas.titulo: From the first round to the prize
texto:
**Who takes part.** In a cooking contest there are **concursantes**, a **jurado** and a **presentador** or presentadora. The **favorito** is the one most people expect to win; the **aficionado** follows the show for fun.

**What happens.** Each **prueba** is a **reto**: a **plato** or **postre** with little time. Before that there are **ensayos**. After the **semifinal**, the **finalistas** reach the final.

**The result.** The **clasificación** says who is ahead. One person is **eliminado**; another is **premiado** with a trip.

**The passive voice.** In the news you often hear **ser + participle**: **fue elegido**, **ha sido premiada**, **será anunciado**. The participle agrees with the subject. With **por** you say who does the action.

**Ser + participle** puts the person or thing that receives the action first: **El postre fue elegido por el jurado.** The participle agrees with the subject: **elegido**, **elegida**, **elegidos**, **elegidas**.

- With **por** you say who does the action (the agent): **por el jurado**.
- It is used in every tense: **fue elegido**, **ha sido elegido**, **será elegido**.
- **Estar + participle** is not passive: it tells the result. **El postre está terminado.**

In daily speech the **reflexive passive** with **se** is very common: **Se anunciará el nombre del ganador.**

ejemplos.estudio: El postre fue elegido por el jurado.
ejemplos.alumno: The dessert was chosen by the jury.

ejemplos.estudio: Los finalistas serán anunciados esta noche.
ejemplos.alumno: The finalists will be announced tonight.

ejemplos.estudio: Se anunciará el nombre del ganador en mayo.
ejemplos.alumno: The name of the winner will be announced in May.

pregunta.texto: Which of these sentences is in the passive voice?

opciones.explicacion: It is active: the jury does the action.

opciones.texto: El postre fue elegido por el jurado
opciones.explicacion: Yes: ser + participle, and «por» says who acts.

opciones.texto: El postre está en el horno
opciones.explicacion: There is no participle: «está» only says where.
It is singular; «los finalistas» is plural.
It is feminine; «los finalistas» is masculine here.

frase.texto: El postre fue elegido por el jurado

piezas.traduccion: The dessert was chosen by the jury

pregunta.texto: What is practising before the real round called?

opciones.explicacion: Yes: «un ensayo» is practice before the real performance.
«Un reto» is something hard you have to overcome.
It is the list that says who is ahead.

pregunta.texto: Which preposition does «premiar» take before the prize?

frase.texto: El ganador será premiado ____ un viaje.

piezas.traduccion: El ganador será premiado ____ un viaje.

opciones.explicacion: «Premiar» does not take «a» before the prize.
Yes: «premiar con» a trip, «premiar con» a trophy.
«Por» gives the reason: «premiado por su receta».

pregunta.texto: Who follows the contest from home out of interest?

opciones.explicacion: The host runs the show on the set.
The finalist competes in the last round.
Yes: the fan follows the show for pleasure, without competing.
